deep.reconstruction:
This is the closing page (numbered 6 by Grothendieck) of a short set of notes on 'épinglages' (pinnings).

Setting, as far as it can be reconstructed from this page and the previous one:
- There is a family of standard models J_n, the cell shapes.
- K is an ordered set equipped with a type function τ_K.
- An M-épinglage of K is a coherent system of isomorphisms u^K_α : J_{τ_K(α)} ≅ K_{≤α}, identifying each lower interval of K with a standard model.
- Page 15 shows that when every element of K lies below one of finitely many maximal elements, the pinning is determined by its values on the maximal elements. The condition is that these values agree on common lower intervals: for ξ ≤ α, β, the two induced isomorphisms J_{τ(ξ)} ≅ K_{≤ξ} must coincide.
- Separately, there is a presheaf category Ĉ, inside which certain 'admissible' objects are singled out. There is a functor X ↦ X̃, presumably sending a presheaf to its pinned poset of cells, or to an associated regular object.

The analogy is with:
- nonsingular (regular) simplicial sets versus ordered simplicial complexes;
- regular CW complexes versus their face posets.

Admissible presheaves are the 'regular' ones, which are faithfully encoded by pinned posets.

The page states three things.
1. Closure. Admissible objects of Ĉ are stable under arbitrary sums. They are also stable under amalgamated sums X ⊔_Z Y when both Z→X and Z→Y are monomorphisms. The functor X ↦ X̃ commutes with these operations; Grothendieck says this 'seems evident'.
2. Finite type. Objects of finite type give objects of finite type under these operations, provided only finite sums are used.
3. NB. When the T's are finite, the admissible objects of finite type of Ĉ correspond exactly to M-pinned ordered sets K that are finite. The T's are presumably the sets of types or automorphism data of the standard cells.

Purpose: to set up a combinatorial, poset-theoretic description of 'regular' cellular presheaves. This is presumably meant as a test or model category of shapes in the stacks / homotopy-types programme, which is the archive context 'Champs 1'.
errors: No outright error. The closure under amalgamated sums correctly requires both maps to be monomorphisms; with only one mono, regularity can fail (degenerate identifications).

The claims are asserted as 'évident' without proof. Commutation of X ↦ X̃ with pushouts along monos relies on the cell poset of a union of sub-objects being the union of the cell posets. That is true in the nonsingular/regular setting, but depends on the precise (unstated) definition of admissible.
The NB's equivalence also needs the M-pinning data to be realisable in Ĉ; this is not checked on the page.

ideas.what: Admissible ('regular') presheaves closed under coproducts and under pushouts along pairs of monomorphisms; the cell-poset functor X ↦ X̃ commutes with these
ideas.modern_name: Closure properties of nonsingular simplicial sets / regular cellular presheaves; face-poset functor preserving unions of subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; nonsingular simplicial sets studied by Fjellbo, Waldhausen–Jahren–Rognes (2013); regular cell complexes by Björner (1984)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses ordered sets, semi-simplicial and cellular models, but not this exact statement as far as known

ideas.what: Equivalence between admissible presheaves of finite type (with finite T) and finite M-pinned posets
ideas.modern_name: Face-poset / cell-poset reconstruction of regular CW or nonsingular simplicial objects (posets with coherent identifications of lower intervals with standard cells)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Björner (CW posets, 1984); Fjellbo / Waldhausen–Jahren–Rognes for nonsingular simplicial sets

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine closure and finiteness remarks concluding a short note on pinned posets as models for regular cellular presheaves. The ideas match folklore and known work on regular CW posets and nonsingular simplicial sets. Nothing appears new.
